#811: flakes under load: admission tests can't attribute an adopted stray; the handoff status-pipe test misses its 20 s stage poll

Two load flakes in capability-broker tests. Both turn up on branches that change no broker code, and both pass when run alone. They have different causes, so each has its own section. A third sighting, of `a_handoff_that_fails_after_the_lookup_starts_no_server`, is already tracked in #743; I've added it there as a comment.

## 1. Admission tests: a stray the engine adopted can't be attributed to one attempt

`engine::broker::admission::tests::every_steps_door_rechecks_the_lease_its_attempt_holds` (crates/brokkr-runtime/src/engine/broker/admission/tests.rs:1396, panic at :1408) fails with:

```
assertion `left == right` failed: {"attempt_id":"…","cleanup":{"reason":"processes 47990, 48017 the engine adopted could not be attributed to one attempt","state":"unresolved"},"effect_id":"effect","reason":"sequence step 'draft': the driver reported success; the attempt is not proven over: …
```

The same shape hits two siblings in the same file: `dispatch_holds_the_lease_while_its_driver_runs_and_releases_it_once_settled` and `an_unprotectable_root_proceeds_unreserved_only_where_nothing_is_at_stake`. Each time, the effect ends `EffectIndeterminate` instead of the expected outcome.

Seen in Brokkr runs (the run ids are journal ids in the controller's forge.db):

| Run | Where | What |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0065-slice-two-unit-u8a2a-see-th-3a0cc19c, seq 3603 | seat, `cargo test -p brokkr-runtime --lib -- engine::broker` | 3 of about 53 parallel runs failed; with `--skip processes::`, 2 of 40; with `--test-threads=1`, 8 of 8 passed |
| 0065-slice-two-unit-u8a2c-see-th-54136b0d, seq 1900 | seat, `runtime --lib engine::` | one or two admission tests on each of three runs, a different one each time |
| fix-round-697b2-for-story-697-sl-b0d595aa, seq 413 | host, full lib | on the branch, 1 of 3 runs failed with two admission tests naming the same stray pid; on main's cut ebe818f7 in a scratch worktree, 1 of 5 failed the same way |
| 0065-slice-two-unit-u8d-see-the--c8d0c134, seq 441 | verify | one failure |
| coverage-round-697b5-for-story-6-0d755969, seq 187 and 231 | boxed verify (namespace box) | twice in a row on a branch with no engine/broker change; on the host 1 of 1 alone and 1226 of 1226 in the full lib |

The U8a2a seat saw `touch` zombies whose parent was the test process. The likely cause (not confirmed) is that the test binary runs several in-process engines in parallel, and they share one process-wide subreaper. A child orphaned by one engine is adopted by the test process, and a concurrently running engine then finds a pid it can't attribute to its attempt. That fits the failures stopping under `--test-threads=1`, and it's the same class as the `Unended(Strays)` flake and #403.

A possible fix: run these tests in their own engine process, the way `brokkr_protocol::process::own_engine::in_its_own_engine` isolates others.

## 2. Handoff: the status-pipe test misses its 20-second stage poll under load

`capability_broker::handoff::a_status_pipe_open_after_the_whole_frame_is_the_handoffs_cause_at_the_deadline` (crates/brokkr-cli/tests/capability_broker/handoff.rs:832) failed in the controller's host exact-coverage gate for story 614 slice 3 while a second lane was building. The panic is at handoff.rs:681–682 in `Handing::at`:

```
no stage of <locator> reached: []
```

`Handing::at` polls 20 seconds for the bootstrap to reach the held-terminal stage. The empty list means that, after 20 seconds, no process of the box existed at all, so the box hadn't started. Run alone on the host, the test passes in 42.87 s, most of which is the test's deliberate 40-second hold. The likely cause (not confirmed) is that the box launch took longer than the 20-second poll on a host saturated by a concurrent build. The poll may need to start from the box's launch, or be bounded by the broker's own startup deadline, rather than a fixed 20 seconds.

Recorded in run landing-pr-for-story-614-slice-3-25d30c0d (seq 1).

## Not in scope here

`a_handoff_that_fails_after_the_lookup_starts_no_server` is tracked in #743. The flakes in #782, #784 and #742 are separate.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)


### Comment, 2026-10-21

More sightings, of both sections and of a third load symptom.

**Section 2 (the 20-second stage poll):** a second test fails in the same `Handing::at` poll. It is `capability_broker::handoff::a_bootstrap_gone_before_the_sender_completes_is_the_handoffs_cause`, failing on GitHub's hosted merge-queue runner in #810's merge group (run 39553256946, job 119067012118):

```
panicked at crates/brokkr-cli/tests/capability_broker/handoff.rs:681:9:
no stage of …/cap-library-docs.json reached: []
```

So this isn't only our workstation: any test that waits through `Handing::at` can miss the 20 seconds on a slow runner.

**A third symptom, `Identity(Expired)` under load:** these admission and sealing tests fail when admission's startup deadline runs out while the host is saturated. That's a different cause from section 1's adopted stray.
- 2026-10-21 09:01–09:03Z, the controller's host check of #814 (head fc012b69) at load average ~31:
  - `admission::tests::{a_box_held_with_no_sealed_reach_is_redirected_by_its_worktree, a_name_that_is_not_utf8_is_an_unknown_participant, a_lease_its_engine_never_released_keeps_refusing_with_the_lock_free}`, each `Err(Identity(Expired))`;
  - `admission::tests::sealing::{a_reseal_that_cannot_link_the_record_that_stood_keeps_it, a_late_release_keeps_the_reservation_that_stood, a_reseal_whose_last_sync_fails_reports_itself_committed}`, the same;
  - `engine::resume_tests::no_gate_topology_is_ever_offered_a_session` ("single gate: the gate did record a confirmed root, and was still offered nothing").
  
  Re-run alone (`--test-threads=1`), all seven passed 3 of 3 in both TMPDIR modes. #814 touches none of these files.
- The peer controller's host gate for #803 saw nine `engine::broker::admission` tests fail with `Err(Identity(Expired))` under load; they were green on rerun.

A fix for this symptom could size these tests' startup deadline for a loaded host, or run them in their own engine as section 1 suggests.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)


### Comment, 2026-10-22

Two more occurrences of the unattributed-stray class, 2026-10-22, both on the workstation under concurrent lanes. Neither branch touches engine/broker:

- `engine::broker::admission::tests::dispatch_holds_the_lease_while_its_driver_runs_and_releases_it_once_settled`, in the host exact-coverage gate for 0089 slice 2a-i (brokkr-store only):
  ```
  panicked at crates/brokkr-runtime/src/engine/broker/admission/tests.rs:1355:5:
  assertion `left == right` failed: {... "cleanup":{"reason":"processes 3417811 the engine adopted could not be attributed to one attempt","state":"unresolved"}, ...}
    left: EffectIndeterminate
   right: EffectSucceeded
  ```
- `engine::broker::admission::tests::every_steps_door_rechecks_the_lease_its_attempt_holds`, once in a landing panel for #717 slice 3b (PR #828): `EffectIndeterminate` where `EffectFailed` was expected, "processes 1603 the engine adopted could not be attributed to one attempt". It passed alone, in the full runtime lib and in the full workspace.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)


### Comment, 2026-10-22

Another instance, 2026-10-22 ~18:10Z, host exact-coverage gate for #717 slice 3c's landing (branch story-717-slice-3c at 7c80db30, which changes no production Rust), with another lane's seat running in parallel:

`engine::broker::admission::tests::dispatch_holds_the_lease_while_its_driver_runs_and_releases_it_once_settled` failed at admission/tests.rs:1355: left `EffectIndeterminate`, right `EffectSucceeded`, cleanup `unresolved`, reason "processes 551763 the engine adopted could not be attributed to one attempt". The other 1,300 runtime lib tests passed. The gate is being re-run.

### Comment, 2026-10-23

First half merged in #848 (9be5d53d). Every admission test whose engine launches a process now plays in an engine of its own (16 guarded; 0 of 20 loops flaked, against 2 of 10 on main). Still open here: the second half, the handoff status-pipe test's 20 s stage poll.


This run takes only the second half of #811: the handoff status-pipe test that misses its 20 s stage poll. The first half (the admission tests) landed in #848.

Rules for this run, one load flake of the sweep in #857:
- Never weaken an assertion. A bound that moves keeps a fail-closed limit and a comment saying why.
- Commit the fix as soon as it builds and the test passes, before any measuring. Your attempt is killed at 2 hours, and on this loaded host one in-suite run of a crate's tests takes several minutes.
- Then measure within a budget: at most 20 runs of the one test alone (filtered to it) and at most 3 in-suite runs, before and after, in 45 minutes at most. Quote the counts you have when the budget ends in the report and in an amended commit message. Never extend the budget, and never revert the fix to measure: earlier attempts on this branch left their measurements under .forge/loops/, so reuse those for the before side.
- The worktree may hold an earlier attempt's uncommitted fix, killed at the 2-hour limit while it was measuring. Read it first, keep what holds and finish it.
- Tests first. If the cause is in production code (a lost stderr, an unflushed exit), fix it there and say so.
- Stay off decision 0065 slice two's open work (#853) beyond the test in question.
- Synthetic fixtures only; the repository is public.
- Commits are unsigned (this worktree sets commit.gpgsign=false); the operator seals the branch before merge. Never push, open a pull request or touch GitHub issues.
- /tmp: a seat's own test run may show tempdir tests failing with `root: "/tmp"`, "up to /tmp" or "recipe 'x' already exists at /tmp/recipes/x". That is an empty /tmp/.git another sandbox on this host leaves, not this branch. Report it by its signature and never stop on it.
- Other timing tests that fail under load and pass alone and in-suite are the sweep's other flakes (#857). Report them; don't fix them here.

instructions.analyze:
# OpenSpec analyze

Judge duplication, ambiguity, underspecification, house alignment, coverage gaps, and inconsistency across proposal, deltas, design and tasks. Treat the realm house as the constitution. Return each finding with severity and its earliest owning artifact; zero findings is consistent.
instructions.clarify:
# OpenSpec clarify

Judge underspecified areas, unquantified language, missing decisions, capability/delta mismatches, and requirements without adequate scenarios. Return every ambiguity with the evidence needed to settle it; zero findings is clear.
instructions.design:
# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.
instructions.implement:
# OpenSpec tasks

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/tasks.md` as numbered groups of checkboxes. Name the requirement served by every task. On return, repair the breakdown and its requirement coverage before implementation resumes.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Archiving a change is the last task and ends its work slice: run the
archive operation named above, which moves the change directory under
`openspec/changes/archive/` and folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`,
the tool's record of archived slices, not the realm's contract.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because the list is the capability's history. The line
is a pointer, not a summary — it names the change and nothing else, and
the why stays in the change directory.
instructions.review:

Create or adopt `openspec/changes/<change>/proposal.md`, then write the capability deltas under `specs/`. The proposal keeps `Why`, `What Changes`, and `Capabilities`; each delta uses requirements and scenarios. On return, answer every finding in the artifacts and keep the proposal and deltas coherent.

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

# OpenSpec tasks

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/tasks.md` as numbered groups of checkboxes. Name the requirement served by every task. On return, repair the breakdown and its requirement coverage before implementation resumes.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `recipes/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.
